To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we adapt an unsupervised tool for acquiring morphological rules to a morphological lexica developed in Alexina; (2) we use this tool to uncover derivational operations; (3) we use these operations to enrich the lexica with derivationally related entries.

we propose an approach for enriching a morphological lexica by automatically adding new entries and links between them, and we apply it on two large-scale lexica for two languages, French and Spanish.

we propose an unsupervised approach to enrich morphological lexica by adding derivational information, and that this method is successfully applied to French and Spanish, two typologically very different languages, and that the resulting lexica have been shown to be useful for various NLP applications.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: how can we enrich morphological lexica through unsupervised derivational rule acquisition?
enriching the coverage of derivational information in morphological lexica, without relying on any prior knowledge of the derivational processes at hand.

enriching morphological resources with derivational links, thus allowing for a better coverage of morphological phenomena and for a more complete description of languages, while also improving their usability.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the approach we present in this paper has the potential to be of interest to both linguists and computational linguists.

this paper presents a novel method for deriving new morphological information from an existing lexical resource and an unsupervised morpheme segmentation tool, without relying on a prior knowledge of possible morphological rules.
our method is a valuable contribution to morphological lexicon development.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are able to enrich a lexicon with new entries and new derivation links between existing ones, without relying on any prior knowledge of the language.

we propose a novel approach to enriching morphological dictionaries with new entries and with links between entries that are derived from existing ones through unsupervised acquisition of morphological rules.

we are able to generate new entries and derivational links in a lexicon without relying on any linguistic knowledge about possible derivational processes, and without relying on any prior knowledge about possible derivations in the lexicon.
The main takeaway from our work is that
unsupervised morpho-lexical acquisition is a promising way to enrich existing morphological lexica.
unsupervised rule induction can be used for enriching existing lexica, and for deriving new entries that are not in the lexicon.
it is possible to automatically enrich morphological lexica, without relying on linguistic expertise, by combining unsupervised morpho-lexical acquisition techniques with existing lexical resources.
